claims.text: ECG for everyone: it can show arrhythmia, conduction abnormality, ventricular hypertrophy, pre-excitation, QT prolongation, Brugada syndrome, ischemia or infarction.
claims.quote: ECG is done for all patients. The ECG may reveal arrhythmia, a conduction abnormality, ventricular hypertrophy, pre-excitation, QT prolongation, Brugada syndrome, pacemaker malfunction, myocardial ischemia, or myocardial infarction

claims.text: Pulse oximetry during or right after an episode; hypoxemia calls for CT angiography to rule out pulmonary embolism.
claims.quote: Pulse oximetry should be done during or immediately after an episode to identify hypoxemia (which may indicate pulmonary embolism). If hypoxemia is present, CT angiography is indicated to rule out pulmonary embolism.

claims.text: Labs only by clinical suspicion, but a pregnancy test for every female of childbearing age.
claims.quote: Laboratory tests are done based on clinical suspicion; reflexively obtained laboratory panels are of little use. However, all females of childbearing age should have a pregnancy test.

claims.text: Echocardiography for unexplained or exercise-induced syncope, a murmur, or a suspected intracardiac tumor.
claims.quote: Echocardiography (either point-of-care ultrasound [POCUS] or a traditional echocardiogram) is indicated for patients with clinically unexplained syncope, exercise-induced syncope, cardiac murmurs, or suspected intracardiac tumors

claims.text: Tilt table testing when history and exam point to vasodepressor or other reflex syncope.
claims.quote: Tilt table testing may be done if history and physical examination indicate vasodepressor or other reflex-induced syncope.

claims.text: Head CT or MRI only for signs of a focal CNS disorder.
claims.quote: CT and MRI of the head and brain are indicated only if signs and symptoms suggest a focal CNS disorder.

claims.text: Dizziness during an ongoing attack: pulse oximetry, fingerstick glucose, a pregnancy test in females, and usually an ECG.
claims.quote: Patients with a sudden, ongoing attack should have pulse oximetry and fingerstick glucose test. Female patients should have a pregnancy test. Most clinicians also do electrocardiography (ECG).

claims.text: Gadolinium-enhanced MRI for acute dizziness with headache, neurologic abnormalities or other signs of a central cause.
claims.quote: generally gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is indicated for patients with acute symptoms who have headache, neurologic abnormalities, or any other findings suggestive of a central nervous system etiology.

claims.text: Audiometry and electronystagmography if bedside hearing or vestibular tests are abnormal or equivocal.
claims.quote: Patients for whom results of bedside tests of hearing and vestibular function are abnormal or equivocal should undergo formal testing with audiometry and electronystagmography.
